paragraphs: Friend, this whole psalm is a prayer, and it is not a small one. It asks God to give the king His own justice and righteousness (Psalm 72:1). It asks for a king whose rule reaches "from sea to sea, and from the Euphrates to the ends of the earth" (Psalm 72:8). Big prayers are allowed, baker, because we are talking to a big God.

Now look at what the king is for. Kings bow and gifts pour in, but then comes that little word "For," and we hear what this king will do. "He will deliver the needy who cry out and the afflicted who have no helper" (Psalm 72:12). The prayer says "their blood is precious in his sight" (Psalm 72:14). So the best kind of power is the kind that stoops down to help the people who have nobody. I think that part is the heart of the whole psalm.

And the prayer doesn't stop at the king. It lifts its eyes and says, "Blessed be the LORD God, the God of Israel, who alone does marvelous deeds" (Psalm 72:18). Then it asks that "all the earth be filled with His glory. Amen and amen" (Psalm 72:19). So when you pray, friend, pray big for the people who need help, and then give the praise to God, because He's the One who does the marvelous deeds.
